senses.gloss: m., mostly pl. מְקַרְקְעֵי (v. קַרְקַע) attached to the ground, real estate, opp. מטלטלא.
units: <cite ref="Yevamot 99a">Yeb. 99ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>עבדא כמ׳ דמי</he> a slave is legally considered as real estate; <cite ref="Bava Batra 150a:6">B. Bath. 150ᵃ</cite> <he>כמקרקעא</he> (Ms. M. pl.).
<cite ref="Bava Batra 150a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>שאני מ׳ דניד וכ׳</he> there is a difference between movable real estate (a slave) and an immovable estate; <cite ref="Bava Batra 68a:6">ib. 68ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 150b:8">Ib. 150ᵇ</cite> <he>כתובה דממ׳ תקינו רבנן</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>דאמ׳</he>) the widowhood which the Rabbis have instituted to be guaranteed by real estate.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 150a:7">Ib.ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>כתובת אשה מ׳ הוא</he> the wife’s settlement is considered real estate; a. fr.
